events.content: `cacheComponents` is on, so the product page can't stay dynamic at the top level. I'll wrap inventory in a Suspense boundary so the title streams first.

raw.name: write_file

events.content: I'll confirm the page type-checks and that the title is no longer blocked on inventory.

The product title now renders immediately, and the live inventory loads behind a Suspense boundary.

app/product/page.tsx was awaiting getInventory() in the page itself. That call uses connection(), and with cacheComponents enabled the whole page stayed dynamic, so navigation could not show "Premium Widget" until the inventory resolved.

The inventory fetch now lives in a child component wrapped in <Suspense>. The heading is part of the static shell, and a "Loading inventory..." fallback shows until the stock count and price stream in.
